h1: Traffic Warrant Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: A missed ticket date in El Paso County turns into a warrant, a second charge and a block on your license renewal. Attorney Robert Navar files with the court to have the warrant recalled and the case reset — without you going to jail and, for a Class C ticket, generally without you going to court.
summaryHeading: Do not ignore an El Paso traffic warrant
summary: A traffic warrant in El Paso is generally a Class C matter. The court can recall it when an attorney files an appearance and the paperwork the court requires — you do not have to be arrested to clear it.
Missing a court date is a separate offense under the Transportation Code, so most people with one warrant have two cases: the original ticket and the failure to appear.
An OMNI hold under Transportation Code Chapter 706 blocks your Texas license renewal until the court clears it; see OMNI hold removal.
Our fee is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional, on top of the flat ticket fee. Start with the free warrant lookup.

sections.heading: The Chain: Ticket, Missed Date, Warrant, Second Charge, License Hold
paragraphs: Every El Paso citation carries an appearance date. If nothing happens by that date — no payment, no plea, no attorney on file — the court sends notice and then issues a warrant. In El Paso Municipal Court that can happen fairly quickly; the Justice of the Peace precincts and the smaller city courts move at their own pace, but they all get there. The result is a warrant on the original ticket plus a new Class C case for failing to appear, each with its own fine and court costs set by the court.

Most people find out one of three ways: a letter from the court, a traffic stop where the officer runs the license, or a trip to the DPS office where the clerk says the license cannot be renewed. That last one is the OMNI hold — the Failure to Appear program the courts report into, which denies renewal until the clerk sends DPS a clearance. None of it is unusual. The point is to handle it on your schedule, not during a stop on Loop 375 at midnight.

sections.heading: What an Attorney Filing Does That Walking In Does Not
paragraphs: When you hire us, we file a notice of appearance and a request to recall the warrant — with an attorney bond where the particular court requires one — in the court that issued it. For a Class C traffic warrant, that filing is generally what the court needs: the judge signs the recall, the clerk pulls the warrant from the active list, and the case is reset to a pretrial docket where we negotiate it like any other ticket. Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised. Our traffic warrant recall page walks through the steps court by court.

You do not turn yourself in, you do not wait in the jail lobby for a magistrate, and for a Class C case you generally do not appear at all. Once the warrant is recalled, the original ticket and the failure-to-appear charge are both still open — and that is where the defense work starts. The failure-to-appear case is often dismissed as part of resolving the underlying ticket; we explain the leverage on the failure to appear defense page. If the hold has already blocked your license, we ask the court to send DPS the OMNI clearance once the case is resolved — see OMNI hold removal.

sections.heading: The Fee for a Warrant, and What the Court Charges Separately
paragraphs: Our warrant fee is simple: $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one, added to the flat ticket fee of $59 in Municipal Court or $69 in JP and the smaller city courts. A single old speeding ticket with a warrant in El Paso Municipal Court is therefore $94 with the warrant recalled and the ticket defended; add-on citations are discounted and each extra warrant is $20.

Court costs are separate and set by the court, depending on the outcome; the court may assess its own warrant fee, and the OMNI program carries a per-case fee the court collects before sending the clearance. We do not charge separately for requesting the OMNI clearance when we are already resolving the case. You can hire online and see the total at checkout before you pay.

faqs.q: Will I be arrested for a traffic warrant in El Paso?
faqs.a: You can be, most often during a traffic stop, which is the reason to act first. For Class C traffic warrants an attorney can file to have the warrant recalled so it is pulled from the active list without you being booked.

faqs.q: How long does it take to lift a traffic warrant?
faqs.a: Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised. The Justice of the Peace precincts and the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts act on the days their judge sits. We tell you as soon as the clerk confirms the recall.

faqs.q: Why does the warrant show two cases when I only got one ticket?
faqs.a: Missing the appearance date is its own Class C offense under the Transportation Code, so the court files a failure-to-appear case alongside the original ticket. Both have to be resolved. The failure-to-appear charge is often dismissed as part of settling the first ticket, though that is up to the prosecutor and the court.

faqs.q: I paid the ticket but DPS still won't renew my license. Why?
faqs.a: The court has to send DPS an OMNI clearance after the case closes, and that step sometimes lags or gets missed — or a second court has its own hold. We can contact the clerk, confirm the case is closed, and request the clearance so the hold drops. See OMNI hold removal.
